subject: Second-order growth curve model syntax question

messages.author: 11a40174db495369
messages.subject: Second-order growth curve model syntax question
parts:
Hi lavaan user group,

I'm learning how to specify a second-order growth curve model (GCM) in lavaan and using the example from the site: https://quantdev.ssri.psu.edu/tutorials/growth-modeling-chapter-14-modeling-change-latent-variables-measured-continuous-indicators

I understand all of the models but have a question about the specification of the 2nd-order GCM--it is the last model in the tutorial (fit5). 

This is the model:
                      
                #latent basis model
                      xi_1 =~ 1*eta1+1*eta2+1*eta3 # intercepts for all latent variables (all constrained to 1)
                      xi_2 =~ 0*eta1 + start(0.5)*eta2 + 1*eta3 #slopes
                      xi_1 ~~ start(.8)*xi_1
                      xi_2 ~~ start(.5)*xi_2
                      xi_1 ~~ start(0)*xi_2
                      xi_1 ~ 0*1 
                      xi_2 ~ 1  '

I understand the x1_1 variable is the intercepts and the x1_2 variable is the slopes. The first eta is set to 0, the 2nd is set to .5 (I think?) and the third is set to 3. 

I'm wondering why the variance of xi_1 is set to .8, and why the variance of xi_2 is set to .5. And lastly why is the covariance between xi_1 and xi_2 set to 0? Why are the values indicated with "start" instead of just stating the value? The tutorial doesn't explain why the variances/covariances are specified this way, and I'm really hoping that someone can shed some light onto the interpretation of these specifications. 

Thank you kindly in advance!

Michaela

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Second-order growth curve model syntax question
parts: in lavaan syntax, when the start() function is used, it is not "setting" or "fixing" the parameter to any specific value. It is defining starting values for the estimation, but the parameters are freely estimated.
xi_2 =~ 0*eta1 + start(0.5)*eta2 + 1*eta3 #slopes

Setting the eta3 slope to 1 is not a typo, this is called the unrestricted growth model, meaning that it is not defining a form, and by estimating the second factor loading is asking the data if that follows a linear form or not. For example if the slope for eat2 is 0.5 means that is follows a linear increase 0, 0.5, 1. But is the slope for eta 2 is 1.5, that means that does not follow a linear increase, as it goes down from eta2 to eta3


xi_1 ~ 0*1

This does seems like an unnecesary constraint. It is fixing the mean of the random intercept to 0, instead of estimating it. Which in growth models you are more commonly interested in estimating it
